transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-12-04 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood); Ruth, Marcus, Nina, Tom

Summary:
Short intake focusing on authz, key management, audit trails, and data retention. Sandstone is leaning toward dedicated but needs clarity on KMS integration, SAML SSO, RBAC granularity, and log export/retention. Redwood team to send artifacts and book deeper infra session.

Topics: SOC2 evidence, ISO alignment, SSO/SAML flow with Okta, RBAC roles, audit logs (WORM vs mutable), encryption (KMS/HSM), data residency & retention windows, hosted vs dedicated network isolation.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE, and Priya's our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Ruth: good, thanks. we've got a short list of compliance items — so we'll jump right in.
[00:17] Marcus: morning. big things for us are the audit trails and KMS integration, also SAML and RBAC.
[00:22] Priya: great, i'll sketch out how our hosted, dedicated, and private options map to those controls — apologies in advance if i mumbles, connection is a bit spotty today.
[00:35] Nina: that's fine. first, SOC2 — do you have a Type II? and is it public?
[00:41] Jordan: yes we do, SOC 2 Type II; i'll share the report and the summary of the control mapping after the call. link in the follow-up.
[00:48] Ruth: and ISO? we're required to show ISO mapping for a couple vendors.
[00:52] Jordan: we have an ISO 27001 statement of applicability, i'll include that. the SOC2 and ISO artefacts are fairly standard but if you want the raw evidence we can do an NDA-based transfer.
[01:05] Marcus: good. next — SSO. we use Okta and need SAML 2.0; we also want SCIM for user provisioning eventually. can Redwood integrate with our IdP and support SCIM?
[01:17] Priya: yes we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and have SCIM-based provisioning; there are a couple of caveats around role sync and attribute mappings that we can show in the technical deep-dive.
[01:29] Ruth: about RBAC: we want fine-grained roles — token-level views, ability to restrict access by model or environment, and audit on who invoked what.
[01:39] Priya: our RBAC model supports org > team > role hierarchies. you can create route-level permissions for endpoints, and we log token-level metadata in the audit trail. caveat: some of the hosted-plan telemetry is aggregated for cost reasons, but Dedicated/Private give you raw per-request logs.
[01:58] Marcus: that's key — we need per-request logs, ideally with request/response hashes, and we also need to retain logs for 5 years for a subset of transactions.
[02:08] Jordan: retention policy is configurable. default retention is 90 days in hosted, but Dedicated lets you push logs to your S3 or to a syslog collector with whatever retention you want. we'll document the export paths.
[02:21] Nina: and can we set immutable retention (WORM) for the subset?
[02:25] Priya: yes — on Dedicated you can export to an S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled; for Private you control the entire storage layer so WORM is possible depending on your infra.
[02:36] Tom: KMS — we currently require customer-managed keys for production PII workloads. can we BYOK? HSM?
[02:42] Jordan: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) workflows. HSM-backed keys are supported if you run Private or if you have an external key proxy in front of Dedicated.
[02:56] Marcus: any exposure to Redwood's control plane? we need assurance that plaintext never lands on Redwood-managed disks.
[03:01] Priya: good question — for Dedicated/Private, the model is that customer data in transit is encrypted, and you can opt into envelope encryption where you hold the DEK in your KMS; we can configure to minimize plaintext residency on our services. Hosted has more managed ephemeral caching; we can show the KV cache lifecycle in the deep-dive.
[03:20] Ruth: you mentioned KV cache — how is that handled, especially for long-context models? can cached context be considered PII?
[03:28] Priya: we do prefix caching and KV pages for attention — best practice is to scrub or not store user PII in cache. we can enable instruction-level tokens for redaction or opt to disable caching per-route for sensitive flows. note: disabling cache increases token cost and latency.
[03:50] Marcus: ok that's the tradeoff we expected. next — audit logs: what format and fields do logs include? are response payloads included?
[03:59] Priya: logs are JSON records with timestamp, request ID, model ID, route, caller identity, token counts, and optionally anonymized response metadata. full response payload capture is optional but by default we do not persist full responses in hosted due to privacy; Dedicated/Private can be configured to persist full responses if needed, subject to retention policies.
[04:25] Tom: we need encryption algorithms spelled out — AES-GCM 256, TLS 1.3, support for RSA-PSS for signatures?
[04:33] Jordan: yes TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256-GCM for at-rest encryption. for signatures we can provide details; i'll include the crypto suite doc in the follow-up.
[04:44] Ruth: network isolation — if we go dedicated, can we do VPC peering and restrict egress?
[04:50] Priya: Dedicated supports VPC peering, private-link-like setups, and strict egress controls. Private on-prem is fully customer-controlled. Hosted uses region-based isolation and IP allow-listing.
[05:03] Marcus: any multi-tenancy risk? we need to ensure no cross-tenant leakage especially in GPU memory and local caches.
[05:11] Priya: our runtime zeroes KV pages on eviction and rotates worker instances between model versions; dedicated capacity pools are single-tenant for compute. we also run nightly attestation checks. there may be transcription artifacts here — but we'll surface the architecture diagram in the deep-dive.
[05:32] Jordan: competitors often claim similar things; FastServeAI's dedicated offering still shares kernel-level libs which made our customer nervous. we can walk you through how we isolate at the hypervisor and process levels.
[05:45] Ruth: legal/contracting — do you have standard DPA language that includes sub-processors and data flow diagrams?
[05:51] Jordan: yes, we have a DPA and sub-processor list; i'll attach both. for custom requirements we can negotiate addenda.
[05:59] Nina: for the POC we want to validate latency and KV cache correctness under our load pattern — can you provide a test harness or runbench?
[06:08] Priya: absolutely — Priya: we have benchmark scripts and synthetic workloads, plus we can run your payloads in a 2-week dedicated POC. we'll need your sample prompts and expected throughput.
[06:22] Marcus: cost controls — we must limit max tokens per call and have per-team quotas.
[06:27] Jordan: we provide route-level quotas, token ceilings, and alerting; you can also sync billing to your org and apply tagging. we'll include a cost-control playbook.
[06:40] Tom: timeline — we're targeting a pilot with legal sign-off in Q1.
[06:45] Ruth: yes Q1 pilot is the goal, ideally Jan.
[06:48] Jordan: great. immediate deliverables: SOC2 pack, ISO summary, RBAC docs, audit log schema, and KMS integration guide. Priya will schedule the technical deep-dive.
[06:59] Marcus: one more — can Redwood sign a CCPA/PDPA attestation?
[07:03] Jordan: we have privacy addenda; i'll add a privacy attestation template to the follow-up.
[07:10] Ruth: perfect.
[07:12] Priya: any blockers from your side to run the POC?
[07:16] Nina: legal needs to see the SOC2; security wants the log schema. procurement wants a ballpark cost for a 2-week dedicated test — not full numbers, just estimate.
[07:25] Jordan: we'll include a POC estimate in the follow-up and propose dates.
[07:29] Tom: ok thanks.
[07:31] Jordan: thanks all — we'll send notes.

Recap (end of call):
- Jordan to send security artifacts (SOC2, ISO, DPA, subprocessor list).
- Priya to schedule technical deep-dive to show KV cache lifecycle, dedicated config, and VPC peering docs.
- Customer to provide retention matrix and sample prompts for POC.
- Proposed POC: 2-week dedicated capacity test focused on latency, KV cache correctness, and audit log export.
